subject: EFL Cup
hook: EFL CUP IS NOT WHAT YOU THINK
angle: Rather than being founded for sporting prestige, the League Cup was created specifically to capitalize on newly installed stadium floodlights and monetize winter weekday evenings.
angle_support: It also took advantage of the roll-out of floodlights, allowing fixtures to be played as midweek evening games.

During the late 1950s, the majority of senior English clubs equipped their grounds with floodlights. This opened up the opportunity to exploit weekday evenings throughout the winter. The League Cup was introduced in the 1960–61 season specifically as a mid-week floodlit tournament to replace the Southern Professional Floodlit Cup.
title: The Strange Reason The EFL Cup Was Invented
description: The EFL Cup wasn't born out of a desire for more silverware or prestigious competition. It was a strategic financial move to utilize new stadium floodlights and maximize weekday revenue.
narration: EFL CUP IS NOT WHAT YOU THINK You picture a tournament built for sporting prestige and glory. It was actually a cynical cash grab designed to monetize empty winter evenings using new stadium technology. By the late 1950s, clubs had installed expensive floodlights to host matches after dark. The League Cup launched in 1960 specifically to exploit these weekday slots, aiming to recoup dwindling attendance revenue lost during the season. It was never about winning trophies; it was about selling tickets.
